doc.title: Josiah "Cie" Frazier and Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-01-18

title: How to end a number and play the break
summary: Cie asks how a drummer ends a blues. Williams explains going to the cymbal, the crush roll and rim shots into the break, and adding double raps while practicing.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Yeah, the role is alright. So how do you end them, you know? How do you end the number when you play the end of the, say, a blues? How do you end the end of that?

Well, I mean, when the band gets ready to go out on it, you're playing on the snare drum. Most likely you're going to be going on the cymbal. Yeah. When you're playing the snare going on, I see like... When you get away from that role, you make sure you're full of the... How do you end it?

Yeah. That's it? That's it. Maybe I'm playing too many of the single beats, you think? No, no, you did it right. It's always good. It's not going along with the song. Let's try that end again. Yeah. Yeah. That's it. That's it.

That's all you can do. Yeah. Well, the first number, it goes when you're playing with the band. Yeah. And the first number, if you're playing your crush roll, you get ready to make that, they're all going to make a single.

How do you do it when you come into the break, you know? Well, you just, you see, when you get to the middle part, you just pick up the rim shot. I'm picking it up. It's all right, I'll pick it up. This will pick up your voice a little bit more if I have it up. Yeah. That's not in your way, is it? No, no, it ain't worth it. You need an ice pair or anything on there? Put an ice if you want. That's all right. Throw the ice on the floor, it won't turn anything. Start it off again. Don't forget to hit this one. Don't forget to hit this one. One, two, three. One, two, three. Now, later on, I mean, as you're practicing, you can make some double raps with your own ideas. You know, when you're with that bass. You know, making a beat like this.
Oh, yeah. Something like that, you know what that? You shot it. And a kind of beat like that.
Let's try it from the chorus.
Da da. Da da da. Da da da da. Da da da da. Da da da da. Three. That's all I do, too.
